Keys are the EXACT skip reason text (a renamed reason is drift too). _engine_built_note: UNMEASURED. The engine-building CI job runs this profile, but the counts below are NOT a measurement of that job: they are copies of the engine-less `default` run and are EXPECTED to be WRONG. That job now DOES set PINEFORGE_ENGINE_CORPUS, cloning the public pineforge-4pass/pineforge-corpus at b40aa8ecbe3caa9ad05244cdfd9ee8138da845e4 (the gitlink the pinned engine commit 4e01e96b5165b5d5e46d72bfbbf88ae6c035a6e9 records), so its corpus tests DO run. It does NOT set PINEFORGE_STRING_SETTINGS_SOURCES, because the population sources that variable would point at are NOT public: this repository carries no fixture for them and the public corpus checkout above has no file matching the sha12 names the test globs, so its six population-source cases skip -- hence that row is 6, not 0. Expect the FIRST engine-built run to FAIL on the other rows and the gate to print the exact rows to write here; paste those rows in to measure this profile. The compile-environment rows (the 'PINEFORGE_ENGINE_INCLUDE not set or invalid...' and 'set PINEFORGE_ENGINE_INCLUDE...' rows, 'engine include / compiler unavailable', 'set PINEFORGE_ENGINE_INCLUDE plus a valid pineforge-engine corpus checkout...', 'PINEFORGE_ENGINE_CORPUS is needed for emitted-byte comparison', 'input receipt corpus pin requires PINEFORGE_ENGINE_CORPUS') must stay 0: building the engine and pinning the public corpus must remove every one -- every one EXCEPT the 'population sources require PINEFORGE_STRING_SETTINGS_SOURCES' row, which stays 6 because the sources that knob points at are not public, so the build cannot remove it (ENGINE_BUILD_KEEPS in tests/skip_gate.py).
